species.description: Famous for deep resonant booming calls produced through esophageal inflation, traveling over 4 km across wetlands.
High-frequency shrill whistle designed to carry over rushing river water and locate partners.
Loud, vigorous song with rapid frequency modulation, harsh churring notes, and melodic whistles.
Continuous rhythmic, churring vocalizations with alternating frequency peaks among reed beds.
Sweet musical warbles with rapid descending pitch slides.
Sharp, persistent piping and yapping calls with steep upward frequency sweeps.
Fast ringing series of high-pitched notes with clean harmonic ladders.
Extremely rapid high-pitched whinnying trill that accelerates in tempo.
Distinctive two-syllable slurred whistle with a sharp upward glide.
Gentle, liquid piping calls with tight frequency-modulated crests.
Sharp, explosive, metallic click-like call.
Bizarre nasal trumpetings, screams, and groaning calls.
Rapid acoustic pulses generated by bill clattering, acting as broadband rhythmic bursts.
Piercing raptor whistles and chattering distress calls.
Raucous, crow-like rolling rasp with heavy mid-frequency concentration.
Low barking, dog-like rhythmic croak repeated at regular intervals.
Classic downward-sloping harmonic quack series.
Low-pitched rasping nasal quack and whistling notes.
Abrupt, explosive squawk with wide harmonic spread.
Harsh, guttural single croak delivered when flushed or territorial.
